fallback.foundation: Foundation primitives have Build, Tools and Testkit reverse consumers, including installed and Wasm contracts.
fallback.testkit: Testkit owns simulator lifecycle, Wasm/probe singletons and installed/server contracts.

exclusions.reason: Focused admission retains host parsers, Cargo tools and the release editor. Build additionally admits its existing simulator and optimizer inputs; the other selected contracts require neither.

Owner-specific lint, documentation, tests and declared reverse-consumer checks replace workspace aggregates. Build retains the real private Wasm-probe consumer; unrelated simulator lifecycle tests remain outside the selected contract.
Shared scripts, hooks, recipes and fixtures are unchanged from the complete three-host baseline; source/configuration changes select the full gate.
Foundation and Build implementations, dependencies and feature contracts are unchanged and have no production edge to Text.
Foundation source and features are unchanged. Selected owner/consumer tests retain their primitive integrations and dependency graphs; Foundation or dependency changes select the full gate.
Text retains its feature/graph checks, YAML profile and actual Tools icp-project consumer in the focused graph/test stages.
The existing normal/build feature graph matrix runs in focused graphs. Tools retains every isolated adapter profile in focused tests; Build has no production edge to Tools or Text.
Public Testkit, simulator/server lifecycle and Wasm probe contracts do not consume Text. The private driver’s Text rendering is exercised in focused tests.

Testkit lifecycle and protocol implementations are unchanged. Build still compiles and installs the real private Wasm probe; Tools retains its typed public consumer without simulator execution. Testkit source or dependency changes select the full gate.
Focused archive qualification uses the same IC Build engine, exact selected public package, normalized source/lock admission and installed archive tests.
Text’s runtime caller is confined to icp-project, exercised separately; the remaining IC adapters do not use Text and are unchanged.
Tools runs every existing isolated adapter profile through focused tests. Build has no production dependency on Tools and its unchanged external adapters.
Wasm inspection does not depend on Text; its source, graph and public identities are unchanged.
The Wasm inspector is an unchanged Foundation application with no dependency on Tools or Build; its source, graph and public identities are unchanged.
